title: barh
summary: Create horizontal bar charts in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: `barh` uses the shared bar rendering path. Supported gpuArray inputs are packed into horizontal bar vertices directly on the plotting GPU context.

description: `barh` creates horizontal bar charts from vector or matrix-style inputs. It returns a bar handle and supports grouped and stacked forms through the shared MATLAB/RunMat plotting handle-property system.
behaviors: Vector inputs create a single horizontal bar series with implicit category positions on the y-axis.
Matrix inputs support grouped and stacked horizontal bar rendering workflows.
The returned value is a bar handle that can be queried and updated through `get` and `set`.
Display names, bar width, and face color participate in the shared plotting object/property model.
RunMat preserves the same fast GPU-backed rendering path as `bar` when inputs and style options can be handled by the shared bar vertex packer.

examples.description: Create a basic horizontal bar chart from a vector
Create grouped horizontal bars from a matrix
Style a horizontal bar object and label it for the legend

faqs.question: How is `barh` different from `bar`?
faqs.answer:
`barh` draws the same bar data horizontally. The y-axis is the category axis and the x-axis shows the numeric values.

```matlab
bar([3 5 2 9]);   % vertical bars
barh([3 5 2 9]);  % horizontal bars
```

faqs.question: How do I create grouped vs stacked horizontal bar charts?
faqs.answer:
Pass a matrix to `barh`. By default, each row becomes a group with side-by-side horizontal bars. To stack them instead, pass `'stacked'`.

```matlab
Y = [3 5 2; 4 6 1; 5 4 3];
barh(Y);            % grouped
barh(Y, 'stacked'); % stacked
```

faqs.question: Can `barh` use explicit category positions?

gpu_residency: `barh` preserves GPU residency where the shared bar geometry pipeline can consume exported buffers directly. Stacked gpuArray charts read values for stacked extent calculation, matching the existing `bar` stacked-bounds behavior, then render through the same GPU plotting path.
gpu_behavior: Horizontal bar rendering shares the same plotting architecture and shader vertex-packing path as vertical `bar`.
The builtin is a plotting sink and fusion barrier.
